standard_prerequisites: Dependent type families over A, sections f of such families, and the dependent action of f on paths (apd), with its definitional behaviour on refl.
The ordinary action of a function on paths (ap) with its definitional behaviour on refl.
Transport along a path and the transconst notation for transport in a constant family, both introduced by the retained context.
Path concatenation and inversion with their definitional behaviour on refl.
core_obligations: Construct, by path induction, for every function f from A to B and every path p in x = y an identification in the identity type of paths in B between apd of f along p and the composite of the transport transconst of f(x) with ap of f along p.
proof_roadmap: Define the type family D over x, y, p by D(x, y, p) = (apd of f along p equals transconst of f(x) concatenated with ap of f along p).
Base case: D(x, x, refl x) reduces definitionally to a type all three of whose constituent paths are refl of f(x), by the definitional behaviour of apd, transport on refl, and ap on refl.
Inhabit the base case by refl of refl of f(x) and apply path induction to obtain an element of D(x, y, p) for every path p, as desired.
difficulty_reason: A single path induction whose base case requires the joint definitional computation of three path operations (apd, transport, ap) on reflexivity.
